texts.label: text
texts.orig: . The GACCS framework (Goals, Audience, Creative, Channels, Stakeholders) keeps teams from doing busywork, drives cross-team alignment, and helps marketers produce more work that your prospects and customers—and coworkers—love. In short, it helps stop marketing work from being a waste of time. I created and evolved this framework while leading marketing at Asana and Carta, and I constantly use it with startups I invest in and advise.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pretty much the number one rule of marketing: Know your audience. If you make something for “everyone,” you are really making it for no one. Including the audience in the GACCS should force you to get specific—and if you just put “users,” you are about four levels too high. This is a great chance to reference those ideal customer personas you made and maybe forgot about, like “Sales Sam” and “Security Shaq.”

texts.orig: If you are struggling to write a GACCS, it might mean you don’t have alignment on your marketing foundation. Your marketing foundation includes having a shared understanding of OKRs or goals, ideal customer personas (ICPs), your addressable market, your overall story, and your primary growth levers. If you don’t have these things, go back and make them. Drive alignment here and you’ll move faster on everything—GACCS writing included.

texts.orig: When to write and share the GACCS
texts.text: When to write and share the GACCS

texts.label: text
texts.orig: GACCS is super-flexible and scalable for any size of team, and it’s helpful for almost any type of marketing work—from a one-off deliverable to a complex campaign. If founders or product, sales, and CS teams want to have a better and more productive working relationship with marketing, suggest that your marketing team share a GACCS with you before they do the work. If you’re a marketer or growth person (or anyone working on user-facing content), use the GACCS on all of your projects to create more impactful work that everyone in the company is proud of.

texts.orig: Why use GACCS?
texts.text: Why use GACCS?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When marketing work is not moving the needle, complicated systems and processes are often put in place to try to solve the problem—these never work:
texts.text: When marketing work is not moving the needle, complicated systems and processes are often put in place to try to solve the problem—these never work:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Someone adds another status meeting across teams to try to get aligned more regularly.
texts.text: Someone adds another status meeting across teams to try to get aligned more regularly.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Biz ops or a chief of staff puts in place an (arduous) process for creating and sharing OKRs across the company—now there are 17 layers of OKRs that are supposed to ladder up to each other that no one looks at.
texts.text: Biz ops or a chief of staff puts in place an (arduous) process for creating and sharing OKRs across the company—now there are 17 layers of OKRs that are supposed to ladder up to each other that no one looks at.

texts.label: list_item

texts.orig: Bonus template: Areas of Responsibility (AORs)
texts.text: Bonus template: Areas of Responsibility (AORs)

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To help the marketing organization work effectively with other teams, I also recommend the AORs framework. When working across teams, too much time is wasted figuring out who you should collaborate with. Marketing has many different subfunctions, so it’s especially hard for other teams to understand the various roles.
texts.text: To help the marketing organization work effectively with other teams, I also recommend the AORs framework. When working across teams, too much time is wasted figuring out who you should collaborate with. Marketing has many different subfunctions, so it’s especially hard for other teams to understand the various roles.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The best solution I’ve found is a shared list of responsibilities across the company, but at the very least across product and customer-facing teams. I learned this system at Asana: areas of responsibility, or AORs.
texts.text: The best solution I’ve found is a shared list of responsibilities across the company, but at the very least across product and customer-facing teams. I learned this system at Asana: areas of responsibility, or AORs.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: With AORs, there is extreme clarity on who owns what.
texts.text: With AORs, there is extreme clarity on who owns what.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I know exactly who to Slack when I need to collaborate, who to invite to the kickoff, and who to ask for help. This also makes filling out the S part of the GACCS much easier.

texts.text: Here’s how it works:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Create a shared list of responsibilities for each employee, grouped by team or sub-team.
texts.text: Create a shared list of responsibilities for each employee, grouped by team or sub-team.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: The main purpose of this list is for other people in the company to be able to look up exactly who owns what, such as product onboarding copy, transactional emails, or web analytics.
texts.text: The main purpose of this list is for other people in the company to be able to look up exactly who owns what, such as product onboarding copy, transactional emails, or web analytics.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: AORs aren’t job titles; those tend to not be specific enough for internal use (I mean—they aren’t really useful just in general . . . but that’s another post).
texts.text: AORs aren’t job titles; those tend to not be specific enough for internal use (I mean—they aren’t really useful just in general . . . but that’s another post).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Instead, include ownership areas where the employee is the directly responsible individual (DRI).
texts.text: Instead, include ownership areas where the employee is the directly responsible individual (DRI).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: If multiple people own the area on the list, you need to get more granular. You have the right level of detail when only one person owns each area.
texts.text: If multiple people own the area on the list, you need to get more granular. You have the right level of detail when only one person owns each area.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Each individual is responsible for keeping their responsibilities updated.
texts.text: Each individual is responsible for keeping their responsibilities updated.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Every time there’s a role or responsibility change or a new hire, this needs to be updated.
texts.text: Every time there’s a role or responsibility change or a new hire, this needs to be updated.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: If two teams are involved on something, such as the onboarding experience, include the owner from each team, like this: “Onboarding—marketing collaborator: Emily” and “Onboarding—product DRI: Lenny.”
